checks.a_analysis: The output document correctly represents the content of the source PDF without any duplication of paragraphs, lists, or headers. Each section of text appears exactly once in the sequence shown in the original document.

The pipeline identifies the main title as a Heading Level 2. While the document lacks subsequent headings (H3, H4) despite having visual sections (which it converted to paragraphs and lists), there are no skips in the hierarchy (e.g., H1 to H3). This is a flat but valid hierarchy for a single-page document.
The source document contains no tables; therefore, no table structures were corrupted in the conversion.

The reading order in the JSON follows the logical top-to-bottom flow of the source PDF, starting with the title and contact info, followed by the specific organization sections (IRIS, USGS, Virtual Earthquake, QCN, ANSS), and concluding with the logos.

The indented sub-items found under major sections like IRIS, Virtual Earthquake, and USGS are correctly identified and grouped as lists in the JSON output. The items are correctly split and maintained their semantic meaning.

The majority of URLs present in the source PDF are converted as plain text spans with formatting (bold/underline) rather than interactive link objects (missing 'href' property). While the email in Element 2 and the 'New version' URL in Element 9 are correctly converted to links, others such as the IRIS homepage, the USGS hazards program, and the Berkeley data center are not clickable in the JSON structure.
